classification.difficultyReason: Intersect the two original logarithmic domains before factoring and cancelling, then sketch the resulting translated logarithm on that retained domain.

inlines.text: Intersect the original domains before using the quotient law.

answer.worked:
Both original logarithm arguments must be positive:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-1&>0\quad\text{so }x<-1\text{ or }x>1,\\x+1&>0\quad\text{so }x>-1.\end{align*}$$
Their common domain is $x>1$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=\ln\left(\frac{x^2-1}{x+1}\right)\\y&=\ln(x-1),\quad x>1\end{align*}$$
The vertical asymptote is $x=1$. For the $x$-intercept, $\ln(x-1)=0$, giving $x=2$. There is no $y$-intercept because $0$ is outside the domain. At $x=3$, $y=\ln2$. Sketch the increasing logarithmic curve through $(2,0)$ and $(3,\ln2)$, approaching $x=1$ from the right. The range is $\mathbb R$.
